points.what: LATAM orders rose 40.2% WoW, contributing 35 orders, 134.6% of the week's total order growth.
points.so_what: LATAM alone accounted for more than all of the week's order growth, offsetting declines elsewhere.

points.what: APAC, the largest region at 44.7% of orders, fell 1.3% WoW and contributed -5 to the week's change.
points.so_what: The largest region declining WoW shows the week's order growth did not come from the biggest source of orders.

points.what: Email and Display orders grew 31.4% and 47.8% WoW respectively, each contributing 11 orders to the week's growth.
points.so_what: Search, which holds 69.9% of orders, contributed only 2 orders to the change, so growth came from smaller channels rather than the largest traffic source.

points.what: AOV fell 5.2% WoW to 83.03, but was still up 5.3% YoY.
points.so_what: With orders up 3.1% WoW, the smaller 1.1% WoW revenue gain shows this week's growth came from more orders rather than bigger baskets.

points.what: Cancellation rate fell 2.8 pp WoW to 13.6%, a notable improvement, but remains up 1.2 pp YoY.
points.so_what: Each point of cancellation is worth 710 in revenue, so the WoW drop helps revenue even though the rate is still worse than last year.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 09 Mar 2026 rose 0.3 pp WoW to 9.5%, though it remains down 1.6 pp YoY.
points.so_what: The WoW rise is a small negative move, but the YoY drop means return-related revenue loss remains lower than a year ago.

points.what: New signups rose 10.3% WoW, a notable increase, but were down 3.7% YoY.
points.so_what: Orders grew 83.1% YoY over the same period, so signup growth continues to lag far behind order growth on a yearly basis.

summary.headline: Orders finished ahead of target at 102.9% but revenue lagged at 90.2%, leaving Q1 at 92.4% of target as the quarter closes with an unusually large order jump.

points.what: Orders reached 855, 102.9% of target, a level flagged as outside the normal 8-week range.
points.so_what: This week's ahead-of-target result is an outlier rather than a new steady pace.

points.what: Revenue was 61356, 90.2% of target, even as orders finished ahead of target.
points.so_what: The gap between orders ahead and revenue behind points to lower value per order as the source of the shortfall.

points.what: Q1 closed at 92.4% of target, the third straight month behind target.
points.so_what: Q2 starts with the quarter's target gap already built in rather than closed.

points.what: New signups rose 10.3% WoW but were still down 3.7% YoY, well behind the 83.1% YoY growth in orders.
points.so_what: New customer growth continues to lag far behind order growth on a yearly view.

points.what: Orders were 855 against a target of 831, an attainment of 102.9%.
points.so_what: The week ended ahead of target, but next week's target rises to 896, above this week's actual, so the pace needs to increase to stay ahead.

points.what: Revenue was 61356 against a target of 68006, an attainment of 90.2%.
points.so_what: This is the same shortfall pattern that has kept revenue behind target through the quarter.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue attainment is 92.4%, and the required weekly revenue run rate for the rest of the year is 79331 against a current 8-week run rate of 57236.
points.so_what: The current pace is well below what's needed, so the full-year revenue target is out of reach without a significant increase in weekly revenue.

points.what: The current 8-week revenue run rate is 57236, against a required weekly run rate of 79331 needed for the rest of the year.
points.so_what: At this pace, the full-year revenue target is out of reach.

points.what: Cancellation rate is still up 1.2 pp YoY despite this week's WoW improvement.
points.so_what: The year-on-year direction remains worse than last year, a risk if the WoW improvement doesn't hold.

points.what: All three months of Q1 (Jan, Feb, Mar) closed behind target.
points.so_what: Entering Q2, the year starts already behind rather than at target.
